overview:
Get metrics from the Stardog service in real time to:

- Visualize and monitor Stardog states.
- Be notified about Stardog failovers and events.
setup:
The Stardog check is not included in the [Datadog Agent][2] package, so you need to install it.

### Installation

For Agent v7.21+ / v6.21+, follow the instructions below to install the Stardog check on your host. See [Use Community Integrations][3] to install with the Docker Agent or earlier versions of the Agent.

1. Run the following command to install the Agent integration:

   ```shell
   datadog-agent integration install -t datadog-stardog==<INTEGRATION_VERSION>
   ```

2. Configure your integration similar to core [integrations][4].

### Configuration

1. Edit the `stardog.d/conf.yaml` file in the `conf.d/` folder at the root of your [Agent's configuration directory][6] to start collecting your Stardog [metrics](#metrics). See the [sample stardog.d/conf.yaml][7] for all available configuration options.

2. [Restart the Agent][8].

metrics.name: stardog.databases.dbname.stats.stalls.l0
metrics.description: The total number of stalls which occurred because the number of files in the L0 level exceeded the hard limit, and all writes must pause because of it.

metrics.description: The total number of stalls which occurred in the L0 level while a compaction was currently running.

metrics.name: stardog.databases.dbname.stats.stalls.pendingCompaction
metrics.description: The current number of stalls which happened while a compaction was pending since the process started or the database was created.

metrics.name: stardog.databases.dbname.stats.writeAmplification
metrics.description: The ratio of bytes written to storage versus bytes written to the database. metrics.description: The maximum amount of memory allowed for the Java heap. Equivalent to -Xmx settings.

metrics.description: The maximum amount of Java heap which is devoted to use by query blocks.

metrics.name: stardog.dbms.memory.mapped.used
metrics.description: The amount of memory currently in use for memory mapped buffers in the Java subsystem. Note that this does _not_ include any memory-mapped usage from native sources (such as rocksdb).

metrics.name: stardog.dbms.memory.native.max
metrics.description: The maximum amount of native memory that the process is allowed to use outside of the JVM. This includes any buffers that are natively created by populated inside the JVM, as well as any memory which is natively allocated (such as rocksdb).

metrics.name: stardog.dbms.memory.native.query.blocks.max
metrics.description: The maximum amount of native (off-heap) memory which is devoted to use by query blocks.

metrics.name: stardog.dbms.memory.native.query.blocks.used
metrics.description: The amount of native (off-heap) memory which is currently being used by query blocks in the memory management system.

metrics.description: the size of a single memory page in the OS.

metrics.name: stardog.dbms.memory.system.pinnedSize
metrics.description: the current amount of memory which is 'pinned' by the operating system, and cannot be swapped out by the process. Note that only some operating systems support this; operating systems which do not support the metric will report -1 for this value always.

metrics.name: stardog.dbms.memory.system.regioncount
metrics.description: The current OS-reported number of regions in use by this process. This number only applies to Operating systems which have a region-based memory system, like OS X (but not Linux or Windows). For operating systems which does not use regional memory, this number will be set to 1.

metrics.name: stardog.dbms.memory.system.rss

metrics.name: stardog.dbms.memory.system.rss.peak
metrics.description: The OS-reported maximum RSS achieved by this process since it started.

metrics.name: stardog.dbms.memory.system.usageRatio

metrics.name: stardog.dbms.memory.system.virtual

metrics.name: stardog.system.uptime
